context: The bus dropped you in a small town and your guesthouse is somewhere nearby, but your phone map is confusing. Today: stopping a local, confirming the way, and finding the kōban.

phrases.jp: すみません、ちょっと{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}ってしまって…
phrases.en: Excuse me, I'm a bit lost...
phrases.note: Say it and trail off: people will usually ask you where you're going.

phrases.jp: この{近|ちか}くに{交番|こうばん}はありますか。
phrases.en: Is there a police box near here?
phrases.note: {交番|こうばん} = small police box. Officers give directions all day; it's normal to ask them.

phrases.jp: {次|つぎ}の{角|かど}を{右|みぎ}ですね。
phrases.en: So it's right at the next corner?
phrases.note: Repeat directions back with ですね to check. You'll hear はい、そうです or a correction.

phrases.jp: {道|みち}の{反対側|はんたいがわ}ですか。
phrases.en: Is it on the other side of the road?
phrases.note: You may also hear {向|む}かい{側|がわ}, same meaning.

phrases.jp: あれ、{道|みち}{間違|まちが}えたかも。
phrases.en: Huh, I might have gone the wrong way.
phrases.note: かも = maybe (short for かもしれない). The を after {道|みち} drops in casual talk.

dialogue_setting: On a quiet street in a small town, asking a local the way.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: すみません、さくらゲストハウスを{探|さが}しているんですが。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, I'm looking for Sakura Guesthouse.

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.jp: ああ、この{道|みち}を{真|ま}っすぐ{行|い}って、{二|ふた}つ{目|め}の{信号|しんごう}を{左|ひだり}に{曲|ま}がってください。
dialogue.en: Ah, go straight along this road and turn left at the second traffic light.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {二|ふた}つ{目|め}の{信号|しんごう}を{左|ひだり}ですね。
dialogue.en: Left at the second light, right?

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.jp: そうそう。{曲|ま}がったら、{突|つ}き{当|あ}たりにありますよ。
dialogue.en: That's it. Once you turn, it's at the end of the street.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: ここから{歩|ある}いてどのくらいですか。
dialogue.en: How long is it on foot from here?

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.jp: 5{分|ふん}ぐらいで{着|つ}きますよ。
dialogue.en: You'll get there in about five minutes.

kanji.where: The red dot on every street map board, station map and mall floor plan. Find it first, then look for your destination.
kanji.related: Related: {案内図|あんないず} map board, {方面|ほうめん} direction (e.g. {駅|えき}{方面|ほうめん} towards the station).

tip.title: No street names: count lights and landmarks
tip.body: Most streets in Japan have no names. Addresses go by area, block and building, like 3{丁目|ちょうめ}5-2, so locals give directions with landmarks and by counting traffic lights. Listen for コンビニ, {信号|しんごう} and {角|かど}. If an address beats everyone, a kōban officer has detailed block maps.

challenge.prompt: You're lost on the way to the bus stop. Tell a passer-by: "Excuse me, I'm lost. Is the bus stop near here?"
challenge.hint: bus stop = バス{停|てい}. near here = この{近|ちか}く.
challenge.model_answer: すみません、{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}ってしまったんですが、バス{停|てい}はこの{近|ちか}くですか。

vocab.note: {道|みち}に{迷|まよ}う = lose your way.
Takes を: {角|かど}を{曲|ま}がる.

extras.title: Landmark words
extras.title_jp: {目印|めじるし}の{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Directions you'll hear, especially in the countryside.

items.jp: {橋|はし}を{渡|わた}って、すぐです。
items.en: Cross the bridge and it's right there.

items.jp: {踏切|ふみきり}の{手前|てまえ}です。
items.en: It's just before the railway crossing.
items.note: {手前|てまえ} = this side of; {先|さき} = past it.

items.jp: コンビニの{向|む}かいです。
ガソリンスタンドの{隣|となり}です。
items.en: It's next to the gas station.

extras.title: At the kōban
extras.intro: Show the address on your phone and use these.

items.jp: この{住所|じゅうしょ}に{行|い}きたいんですが。
items.en: I'd like to go to this address.

items.jp: {地図|ちず}に{書|か}いていただけますか。
items.en: Could you draw it on the map for me?

items.jp: {地図|ちず}の{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ってもいいですか。
items.en: May I take a photo of the map?
items.note: Kōban often have big hand-drawn local maps on the wall.
